title: The 'numeral cryptogram' after the reader Ioannes' note in a Greek Gospel lectionary (Trinity College Cambridge O.4.22, f. 248v): not a cipher, a Paschal full-moon table

steps.what: Fetched f. 248v from the CUDL IIIF server as full-resolution region crops (page image 503, 4,797 x 7,350 px); images are CC BY-NC 4.0 for download and are not committed here.
Read the three lines on contrast-enhanced crops and collated with CUDL: same 38 numerals; doubts at counts 5, 14 and 18; the minuscule 'φον' and 'μου' at the line ends are the end of the clear note.

Split as Daniel suggested into a running count 1-19 and a value each. Values never exceed 30 and value + count repeats with period 3 (13, 34, 23) for counts 3-14, the signature of a sequence stepping by 11 or 19 modulo 30: the Paschal full moons of the 19-year cycle.

Measurement frozen by sha256 before running (results/measure.py): the 19 values against the Julian computus (21 March + (19(GN-1)+15) mod 30) with the historical Byzantine offset GN = n + 3: 19 of 19 agree. 200 shuffles of the values over the counts: at most 4 of 19 (mean 1.0); the 18 other offsets: 0 of 19 each. The hypothesis was found by looking at the values, so this confirms on the same 38 numerals; there is no other text to hold out.

Independent check by a project session (claude-fable-5-2), which reached the same identification from the CUDL transcription before seeing PR #690: grouping checked on full-resolution crops by the overlines; independent_check.py computes the table from the AD year and matches 19 of 19 values in pairs.tsv.

outcome.method_basis: The numerals are a computus table, not an encipherment: each of the 19 counts is followed by its Paschal full-moon date, 19 of 19 as the standard Byzantine reckoning gives them.

credits.note: Brice Dudout, with a Claude agent (claude-opus-5-5): transcription from the CUDL images and identification of the series as the Paschal full-moon table of the Byzantine lunar cycle.

texts.label: O.4.22 f. 248v, the 19 pairs
texts.summary: Table of the legal Passover (Paschal full moon) for each year 1-19 of the Byzantine lunar cycle: 1: 2 April, 2: 22 March, 3: 10 April, ... 19: 13 April.
texts.note: Preliminary: not yet reviewed by a second reader. No name or message is hidden in the numerals.

outcome.fraction_read_source: pairs.tsv: all 38 numerals form 19 pairs, each value equal to the computus date (results/measure_output.txt).

gaps.detail: The computus fixes their values; the doubt is on letter shapes in faint ink only.

outcome.notes: Corrects the CUDL description and catalogue entry 2902: the series does not hide the teacher's name. The note of Ioannes the reader is a separate clear text; its last words 'φον μου' run on into the free space to the right of the table.
